name: PEARSON
description: PEARSON returns the Pearson product-moment correlation coefficient for two data sets, identical in result to CORREL.
tldr: Pearson correlation coefficient between two arrays (same as CORREL).

parameters.name: array1
parameters.description: The first set of independent (or paired) numeric values.

parameters.name: array2
parameters.description: The second set of numeric values, the same length as array1.

basicExample.explanation: Identical to CORREL on the same data; the coefficient is near 1, a strong positive linear relationship.

advancedExamples.title: Correlation from ranges
advancedExamples.description: Both ranges must have the same number of points
advancedExamples.explanation: Pairs each row; mismatched sizes cause #N/A. The result equals CORREL on the same inputs.

advancedExamples.title: Verifying equivalence with CORREL
advancedExamples.description: Show the two functions return the same value
advancedExamples.explanation: PEARSON and CORREL use the same Pearson formula, so they always agree.

howItWorks: PEARSON computes r = Σ((x - x̄)(y - ȳ)) / sqrt(Σ(x - x̄)² · Σ(y - ȳ)²). The result is bounded by -1 and 1. It is mathematically and functionally identical to CORREL; text, logicals, and empty cells are ignored in each array.

howToSteps.name: Arrange paired data
howToSteps.text: Put the two related series in equal-length ranges.

howToSteps.name: Read the coefficient
howToSteps.text: Values near 1 or -1 indicate strong linear association.

limitations: Measures only linear association, like CORREL; non-linear links may show ~0.
Both arrays must contain the same number of data points, or #N/A is returned.
If either array has zero variance, the function returns #DIV/0!.

commonErrors.cause: The two arrays have different numbers of data points.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure array1 and array2 are the same length.

commonErrors.cause: One of the arrays has no variance (all values equal).
commonErrors.fix: Use data with variation, or check for constant columns.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PEARSON works identically in Google Sheets and equals CORREL.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same result as Excel; CORREL is also available and equivalent.

faq.question: Is PEARSON the same as CORREL?
faq.answer: Yes. Both Excel and Google Sheets return the identical Pearson coefficient for the same inputs.

faq.question: Why does PEARSON exist if it equals CORREL?
faq.answer: It is provided for compatibility and familiarity with statistical notation; the result is the same.

faq.question: What does a correlation of 0 mean?
faq.answer: No linear relationship; a non-linear relationship may still be present.
